3.0.s.en: (1) The peace offering from the herd

3.0.0.en: The peace offering means obtaining peace with God. It signifies Christ, who by His redemption restored peace between us and God by taking away sin, and it is the only sacrifice of which the one who offers it is permitted to eat, that is, to partake with God in it, so it signifies Holy Communion, partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord.

3.0.1.en: It may be of the herd or of one of the other animals, but it must be without blemish, that is, without defect, because Christ, whom it signifies, is without sin. The herd signifies giving, since it gives milk and meat. It is noted that the burnt offering mentioned in (ch. 1) is required to be a male because it is a symbol of Christ, who pleased the Father, whereas the peace offering may be male or female, because it signifies the sharing of the believer, male or female, in partaking of the Body of Christ.

3.0.2.en: The peace offering is not to be of birds, because of the small quantity of fat in them to be offered to God on the altar (it is also mentioned in ch. 7, 17, 22, 23). The peace offering was mostly voluntary, expressing a person's thanks and love toward God, as in (ch. 7:16-21; 22:21-25), and sometimes the Law prescribed it, as in the sacrifice of consecration offered at the ordination of the priests (Ex 29:19-28; ch. 8:22-32) and the peace offering offered at the Feast of Pentecost (ch. 23:19, 20). The peace offering was preceded by a sin offering (ch. 8:14-22; 9:3, 4), and this signifies that the Sacrament of Communion is preceded by the Sacrament of Confession.

3.1.0.en: He shall lay his hand upon the head of his offering: to declare his thanks to God, who will allow him to eat of the blessed sacrifice offered to God, which signifies Christ.

3.1.1.en: And kill it at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: that is, before the bronze altar, because Christ gives us His salvation in the Church.

3.1.2.en: And Aaron's sons the priests shall sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about: the priests receive the blood in vessels and sprinkle it around the altar as a symbol of the salvation of Christ offered to the whole world from His holy altar, where we partake of His Body and Blood by means of the priests of the New Testament.

3.2.0.en: Offering made by fire: an offering burned with fire.

3.2.1.en: Here the best part of the sacrifice, the fat, is burned as thanks to God, for thanksgiving must be from the whole heart and all the senses, outwardly and inwardly, and with the best of a person's abilities.

3.3.0.en: Flanks: the two sides at the waist.

3.3.1.en: The caul above the liver: the smaller lobe of the liver.

3.3.2.en: Offered to God also, along with the fat, which is the richest part of the sacrifice, are the inwards, which are the two kidneys and a part of the liver and the fat that is on them, and they signify the offering of the depths of the believer to God. All of this is burned on the altar, and God rejoices in this love.

3.3.3.en: Offer thanks to God from all your heart for His kindnesses, for no gift lacks increase except the one without thanks, and do not look upon the favors of God as ordinary things, but thanks must be offered for them.

3.4.s.en: (2) The peace offering from the flock

3.4.1.en: Lamb: sheep, that is, those that have wool.

3.4.2.en: Peace offerings may be offered from the flock with the same ritual as the offering of cattle mentioned before in (vv. 1-5).

3.5.0.en: The rump: fat at the end of the tailbone, which is the fat tail, that is, the tail of the sheep.

3.5.1.en: These fats are burned with the two kidneys on the altar according to the ritual mentioned before.

3.5.2.en: God rejoices in your gifts, great or small, whatever their kind, because they express your love. So offer Him of your time and your talents and your various abilities to show your sonship to Him, and know that His fatherly love will give you more than you ask or think.

3.6.s.en: (3) The peace offering from the goats

3.6.0.en: Here the offering is from the goats, and the same ritual is repeated as explained before and with the same meanings.

3.7.0.en: The fat and the blood are the richest and most precious part of the sacrifice, so they are offered to God, and it is not permitted for a person to trespass upon the portion set apart for God, in addition to the health harms of fat and its being easily spoiled and its transmitting microbes. Likewise the blood, which represents the soul of the animal and its life, which belongs to God alone, and drinking blood also transmits diseases and stirs up a person's ferocity and lusts. The Christian Church in the first Council of the Apostles (Acts 15:28, 29) decreed that Christians are not to drink blood.

3.7.1.en: Be calm and gentle in your character, for gentleness is among the fruits of the Holy Spirit, while ferocity and aggression are fruits of evil.

4.0.s.en: (1) The sin offering of the priest

4.0.0.en: Commandments of the Lord concerning things which ought not to be done: things that the Lord forbids to be done.

4.0.1.en: God declares His law to the priest and the servant, and they declare it to the people. The sin offering was established for the one who sins through ignorance or weakness or forgetfulness in carrying out God's commandments, and it shows the work of Christ in forgiving our sins, whereas the one who sins deliberately, unless he repents like David (2 Sam 12:1-15), is put to death (Num 15:30). This chapter mentions some kinds of sin offerings, which are:

4.0.2.en: 1- If a priest falls into sin.

4.0.3.en: 2- If the people fall into sin.

4.0.4.en: 3- If a ruler falls into sin.

4.0.5.en: 4- If one of the individuals of the people falls into sin.

4.0.6.en: The discussion of the sin offering extends in the fifth chapter to (v. 15), where it speaks of examples of the sin offering and how those who are not able offer this sacrifice. This sacrifice was offered in the ritual of the ordination of the high priest and the priests (Ex 29:1-14), and for the purification of a woman after childbirth (ch. 12:6), and in the cleansing of those sick with diseases such as leprosy (ch. 14:19) and the bleeding and issue of men and women (ch. 15:14, 15, 29, 30), and at the feasts such as the Feast of Pentecost (ch. 23:19) and the Feast of Tabernacles (ch. 23:33-36......). It is noted that the sin offering whose blood is brought into the sanctuary is burned entirely with fire, whereas the one whose blood is not brought into the sanctuary is eaten from by the priest. The sacrifice whose blood is brought into the sanctuary is:

4.0.7.en: 1- The sin offering for the priest.

4.0.8.en: 2- The sin offering for the whole congregation of the people.

4.1.0.en: Sin according to the sin of the people: the people stumble by his sin.

4.1.1.en: If the sinner is a priest, meaning the high priest, his error is a cause of stumbling to all the people, so his sin offering is a bull. We will notice that the measure of the sin offering is determined according to the person who sins, so it is greater if he has a greater standing, such as the priest. If a person sins against his neighbor, he can make restitution to him for what he damaged for him (Ex 22:1). But here it speaks to us of sin directed toward God, which is atoned for only by the blood of Christ, whom this sacrifice signifies, so no compensation is given, but the sacrifice that signifies the unlimited sacrifice of Christ that atones for us.

4.2.0.en: The laying on of the hand here, on the head of the bull, is to transfer the sin from the sinner to the sacrifice when he confesses it before the Jewish priest, because Christ acted on our behalf in bearing our sins to exact their punishment in Himself, whereas the laying on of the hand in the burnt offering and the peace offering is for the union of the one who offers it with the sacrifice, to obtain its merits and its blessing.

4.3.0.en: Sprinkle: to sprinkle with the tip of his finger.

4.3.1.en: The veil of the sanctuary: the curtain that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies.

4.3.2.en: The priest is responsible before God for his errors, so he enters with the blood of his sacrifice before the Holy of Holies, which is the dwelling of God, to make atonement for them. And the sprinkling on the veil seven times is so that the priest may be sure that the blood of the sacrifice has atoned for his sin, so that he does not doubt the forgiveness that opens the way for his return through the veil to God, because the number seven represents perfection. The veil signifies the sin that separates man from God, which Christ removed by His death on the Cross. The number seven, which signifies the complete week, also shows that forgiveness includes the sinner throughout his life with no turning back on God's part.

4.3.3.en: It is noted that the ordinary person sprinkles the blood of his sacrifice around the bronze altar, whereas the priest sprinkles it on the veil that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies, because the priest is responsible for the service and his sin is greater than the sin of any ordinary person since it is a cause of stumbling to others, so he asks forgiveness from before the Holy of Holies, which signifies the sanctuary and its service.

4.4.0.en: The altar of incense points to prayer that rises like incense before God, and its horns point to its power. Therefore the putting of the blood on the horns of the altar shows the power of the blood of the sacrifice to stand before God as a guarantee of forgiveness. And the pouring out of the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering, which signifies the Cross, points to the death of Christ and the end of His life on the Cross as an acceptable sin offering. The twofold work of the blood, within at the altar of incense and without at the altar of burnt offering, moves us to love Christ who brought us back to the Father, so that we hate the sin that shed His blood and drove us outside.

4.5.0.en: All the fat is gathered with the inwards, that is, the two kidneys and a part of the liver, to be burned on the altar as we mentioned in the peace offering (ch. 3:3, 4).

4.6.1.en: The whole bullock: all the rest of the flesh of the bull.

4.6.2.en: Where the ashes are poured out: where the ashes are thrown outside the camp.

4.6.3.en: The camp: the place where the tents of the people are pitched and where they dwell.

4.6.4.en: The burning of the skin of the bull and its flesh and all the rest of it is outside the camp in a clean place, where it is laid on wood and burned in the place of the ashes, to show what happened to Christ when He bore our sins, for the Father hid His face from Him, and all the people rejected Him and drove Him outside their concern and asked Pilate to crucify Him, and He was crucified outside Jerusalem. For sin makes a person rejected by God and men.

4.6.5.en: It is noted that in the case of the priest's sin the whole animal is burned except the fat offered to God, whereas in the other cases of the sin offering the priest takes the skin and a part of the flesh.

4.6.6.en: Sin corrupts your life and destroys it and makes you rejected by God and men. So do not be deceived by its beauty or share in it with others, however many they may be, but let the salvation of your soul and the pleasing of God be your only goal, and you will be able to give up and trample and reject any sin.

4.7.s.en: (2) The sin offering of the whole congregation

4.7.0.en: Sin through ignorance: they sinned unknowingly, that is, they did not know that what they did was wrong.

4.7.1.en: Hid from the eyes of the assembly: the congregation of Israel did not know that what they were doing was wrong.

4.7.2.en: The sin is known: they discovered by the grace of God that what they had done was wrong against God. The error here is the error of all the people, and those responsible for it are the leaders of the people, so they act on behalf of the people in confessing the sin by laying their hands on the head of the sacrifice.

4.8.0.en: It is noted that the atonement for the sin of the high priest is the same as the atonement for the sin of the whole congregation of the children of Israel, that is, by offering a bull. This confirms the gravity of the priest's sin and the necessity of scrutinizing his conduct so that he does not cause others to stumble. The ritual of offering this sacrifice is the same as the ritual of offering the sacrifice for the sin of the priest, as mentioned in (vv. 3-12).

4.8.1.en: If you are a father or a mother or a servant or responsible anywhere, you are required before God for those for whom you are responsible, to teach them how to live with God and to guide them to keep away from sin. If they accept your word, you have gained their souls, and if they do not accept, their sin is on their own heads. But do not despair of their salvation throughout your life, and offer them your love and guidance and ask God to draw them to repentance and life with Him. And do not be troubled if all those around you insist on sin, but hold fast to the truth and pray for them and guide them gently and firmly as God guides you, in order to draw their hearts to repentance, even if after a while.

4.9.s.en: (3) The sin offering of a ruler

4.9.1.en: The sinner here is a civil ruler among the leaders of the people, so the value of the sacrifice is lowered and it becomes a male kid of the goats, and the sinner performs the same ritual explained before.

4.10.0.en: The sin offering for the ruler differs from the sin offering for the priest (vv. 3-12) in two matters:

4.10.1.en: 1- The priest smears the blood on the horns of the bronze altar, which signify the power of the salvation given by God to His children, and this altar is in the outer court, whereas in the case of the priest's sin he anoints the horns of the altar of incense that is inside the Holy Place, because his sin is greater, for he is the servant of God who enters the Holy Place.

4.10.2.en: 2- The sin offering of the priest, after the burning of the fat, has its flesh and everything in it burned outside the camp, whereas in the case of the ruler's sin the priest eats its flesh, and this assures the one who offers it that God has forgiven his sin, as proved by the eating of it by God's priest.

4.10.3.en: If you, beloved reader, are a servant, feel your responsibility for the sin of your people and share with them in bearing it, by caring for them and guiding them and sympathizing with them and praying for them.

4.11.s.en: (4) The sin offering of individuals of the people

4.11.0.en: If the sinner is an individual of the people, his sacrifice is a female goat, because its price is less than the male, since his sin is less than the sin of the ruler or the priest, and the same ritual and meanings as the sacrifice of the ruler are repeated.

4.12.0.en: Lambs (sheep) were cheaper than goats at that time, so if he is not able to buy a female goat he buys a ewe, that is, a female sheep. The ritual of this sacrifice is the same as the ritual of offering the female goat or the sin offering of the ruler.

4.12.1.en: Let each of us know his sins and grieve over them and repent, and God will forgive them to him and be pleased with him, and he will partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord, which gives salvation for us and forgiveness of sins and eternal life to the one who partakes of it. The sin offering and the trespass offering

5.0.s.en: (1) Examples of sins and the necessity of confession

5.0.0.en: The inspired text gives three examples of sins that a person commits through ignorance, so that the one who commits them needs to offer a sin offering when he learns of them and repents. The first is if a person hears the voice of swearing and is a witness, whether he has seen or known of it, and the one who gave the testimony swore to confirm his testimony, and he had seen or heard the truth and did not correct the error with true testimony. In this case he is guilty, because he took part in the judgment against an innocent person, so he offers a sin offering.

5.1.1.en: Hidden from him: he did not know.

5.1.2.en: The second sin is if he touches the carcass of a wild beast or a cattle or an insect, or the body of a man, or anything of his uncleanness, such as the belongings of the leper (ch. 13) or one who has an issue or a woman with an issue of blood (ch. 12), and he did not notice it. This one also offers a sin offering.

5.2.1.en: The third sin is if a person is hasty and swears, whether to do good to another or to do him harm, and he did not know that what he swore by conflicted with one of God's commandments and His law, and then someone informed him of this error into which he had fallen, so he needs to offer a sin offering.

5.3.1.en: In the three preceding cases, the offender should confess his error before the priest, offering a ewe or a female goat as a sin offering as explained before (ch. 4). This shows the importance of the Sacrament of Confession before partaking of the sacrifice of Christ on the altar, that is, His most holy Body and Blood.

5.3.2.en: Beware of rushing into speech or action lest you fall into sin... Listen well and pray to God and seek the counsel of your father of confession as much as you can, and God will protect you from many sins.

5.4.s.en: (2) The sin offering for those who are not able

5.4.0.en: The poor man offers two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, and their choice is as a symbol of purity and meekness, as explained before (ch. 1:14-17). And since it is difficult to separate the fat from the flesh in birds, one of them is taken in place of the fat and is burned entirely, so it is called a burnt offering although it is a sin offering, and the second, in place of the flesh, is the priest's portion for him to eat of it, so that the one who offers it is assured that his sacrifice has been accepted and his sin forgiven, and so that the priest may learn to accept the gift of the poor man however small, because he is the servant of the poor and the rich.

5.4.1.en: And the wringing off of the head without dividing it asunder is because it is written of Christ that not a bone of Him shall be broken.

5.5.0.en: Ephah: a grain measure with a capacity of 23 liters.

5.5.1.en: The one who cannot afford to buy the two doves may offer a small quantity of fine flour as a sin offering. But to distinguish it from the grain offering mentioned in (ch. 2), he does not put oil or frankincense on it, which are put on the grain offering and signify the work of the Holy Spirit and prayer, because the flour here does not signify the life of Christ on earth but bears the sin of the sinner. The priest burns a handful of it, and it mingles with the blood of the sacrifices on the altar and becomes a sin offering mixed with the blood necessary for forgiveness to take place, and the priest takes the rest as food for himself.

5.5.2.en: God welcomes my repentance and does not want to place on me a material burden that would hinder me from it, because He has no pleasure in the death of the sinner, but that he return and live. So what hinders me from practicing a life of repentance? However great my weakness or the difficulty of my circumstances, I can with God's help repent, and God accepts my return to Him even with a short prayer and a confession before the father of confession.

5.6.s.en: (3) The trespass offering for an error directed against God

5.6.2.en: Shekel of silver: a silver coin weighing one shekel.

5.6.3.en: Shekel of the sanctuary: an exactly accurate shekel kept in the sanctuary, whose weight is double the ordinary shekel.

5.6.4.en: This is the fifth sacrifice, and it points to the work of Christ in forgiving our sins directed against God, and it is of two kinds:

5.6.5.en: 1- Trespass against God and His temple and His holy things.

5.6.6.en: 2- Some grave trespasses against men, which also include trespass against God, as in (ch. 6; ch. 14:12; ch. 19:20).....

5.6.7.en: In these verses it speaks to us of sins directed toward God, and the value of the ram of the sacrifice is determined by the priest according to the harm that has come upon God's holy things. The priest also determines the value of the appropriate compensation, apart from the value of the sacrifice, and the fifth part of the value of the harm is added to the preceding, to remind a person to sanctify his five senses that were defiled by the trespass, so that he does not sin again by them.

5.6.8.en: The trespass here is referred to as being through ignorance, because the Lord's ordinances are many and a person may be unaware of some of them. And the error in the holy things of God is either through ignorance in fulfilling His law, such as not offering the silver for the firstborn or not offering the firstfruits and the tithes, so the priest estimates the amount that should have been offered to God and adds a fifth to it, and he gives it to the priest, and he also offers a ram to make atonement for him.

5.7.0.en: Trespass: transgression against the rights of God.

5.7.1.en: Trespass: transgression or violation or guilt.

5.7.2.en: Among the examples of the Lord's prohibitions against which a person may trespass: eating of the parts of the sacrifice of which eating is not permitted (ch. 22:10-14), or using an animal that has been vowed to God (Deut 15:19). The sacrifice here is mentioned before the compensation because the error is directed against God, who does not give priority to material things. It is noted in the trespass offering that it is a ram and not a ewe, because the price of the ram is higher, for trespass is graver than sin because it is directed to God, so a more costly sacrifice is offered to show the heinousness of the sin.

5.7.3.en: If you sin, repentance is not enough, but compensation for the damages of the error is necessary, otherwise being content with repentance would carry laxity and an escape from the consequences of sin.

5.7.4.en: The trespass offering and the laws of the sacrifices
